rows.source: HSE major accident hazard pipeline integrity
rows.verified: HSE regulates health, safety and integrity issues for natural-gas and other applicable pipelines in Great Britain, territorial waters and the UK Continental Shelf.

rows.source: HSE major accident hazard pipeline integrity
rows.verified: HSE expects pipeline dutyholders to apply relevant good practice as a minimum when demonstrating legal compliance.

rows.source: HSE major accident hazard pipeline integrity
rows.verified: New pipeline plant and situations should apply current good practice, while existing systems must apply it to the extent needed to satisfy the law and ALARP.

rows.source: HSE major accident hazard pipeline integrity
rows.verified: Established standards for design, operation and maintenance can be used to demonstrate that major-accident pipeline risks are ALARP.

rows.source: HSE major accident hazard pipeline integrity
rows.verified: Alternative standards or guidance may be acceptable where the dutyholder can demonstrate an equivalent level of safety.

rows.source: HSE major accident hazard pipeline integrity
rows.verified: A gap analysis should be carried out when relying on alternative standards or recommendations.

rows.source: HSE major accident hazard pipeline integrity
rows.verified: Separate recognised standards address onshore steel pipelines, subsea pipelines, flexible pipe and high-pressure gas transmission.

rows.source: HSE major accident hazard pipeline integrity
rows.verified: Pipeline defect assessment may use recognised fitness-for-service and corrosion-assessment methods, supported by appropriate inspection and repair procedures.

rows.source: HSE major accident hazard pipeline integrity
rows.verified: Pipeline integrity risk depends on fluid, pressure, route, material, age, corrosion, geotechnical loads, third-party activity, inspection quality and emergency arrangements.

rows.source: HSE major accident hazard pipeline integrity
rows.verified: MAH-pipeline evidence is asset-, fluid-, route-, condition- and lifecycle-specific and is not an exact parcel-level release or consequence probability.

rows.source: HSE MAH pipeline lifecycle notifications
rows.verified: The Pipelines Safety Regulations 1996 require major-accident-hazard pipeline operators to provide HSE with information at defined lifecycle stages.

rows.source: HSE MAH pipeline lifecycle notifications
rows.verified: Regulation 20 covers notification before construction, regulation 21 before use, and regulation 22 operator changes or other significant changes.

rows.source: HSE MAH pipeline lifecycle notifications
rows.verified: Construction of a new MAH pipeline should not begin until HSE has been notified at least six months before the start of construction.

rows.source: HSE MAH pipeline lifecycle notifications
rows.verified: HSE requires 14 days' notice before a MAH pipeline is first brought into use or returned to use after being taken out of commission.

rows.source: HSE MAH pipeline lifecycle notifications
rows.verified: A change of MAH pipeline operator must be notified to HSE within 14 days of the change.

rows.source: HSE MAH pipeline lifecycle notifications
rows.verified: Significant modifications under regulation 22(2) generally require at least three months' notification.

rows.source: HSE MAH pipeline lifecycle notifications
rows.verified: Notifiable changes can include operating-pressure limits, fluid composition, materials, equipment, routing and emergency-shutdown-valve position.

rows.source: HSE MAH pipeline lifecycle notifications
rows.verified: End-of-use notifications should describe the timetable and measures for decommissioning, dismantling, abandonment or otherwise making the pipeline permanently safe.

rows.source: HSE MAH pipeline lifecycle notifications
rows.verified: Notification duties depend on whether the pipeline is MAH-classified, the lifecycle stage, the scale of change, the operator identity and the effect on risk.

rows.source: HSE MAH pipeline lifecycle notifications
rows.verified: Pipeline-notification evidence is project-, operator-, modification- and lifecycle-specific and is not an exact parcel-level safety probability.
